title: Foundations and Decision Signal - Company All-Hands
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on operational foundations: stability incidents and mitigations, product prioritization for next 8 weeks, headcount and hiring cadence, and a leadership decision on expanding private deployment support. Quick Q&A and concrete action items at the end.
topics: Private deployment roadmap and compliance gaps
Cost/perf tradeoffs: batching and KV caching experiments
Hiring: SRE and Platform engineering needs
Leadership decision: pilot dedicated customers vs pause

Samir Bose: Run 2-week KV cache benchmark vs baseline and share spreadsheet (due 2025-09-29)

Ravi Shah: Deliver quick internal quality-signal for quantized model performance on private infra (due 2025-09-26)

transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2025-09-16
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Claire Jensen, Aisha Patel, Marco Alvarez, Tess Nguyen, Ravi Shah, Samir Bose, Jordan Kim
Recording: yes (auto)

---

[00:00] Claire Jensen (CEO): Okay, good morning everyone. Let's get started. Thanks for carving time. We got a packed agenda but I want to be explicit — this is about decisions and next steps, not just updates. Aisha, quick ops note before we jump in?

[00:18] Aisha Patel (COO): Yep, thanks Claire. Quick high level: August had a few reliability blips — primarily around KV cache misses and an autoscaler thrash on Dedicated. We've got postmortems in flight but want the leadership alignment on two pieces: immediate mitigation for tail latency, and whether we fast-track additional headcount for SRE.

[00:37] Marco Alvarez (VP Eng): To add, some of the thrash came from a config mismatch when we rolled a new batching policy. There was a small race in the router config that made capacity estimates jump. We rolled rollback at 2am——which, yeah, not great.

[00:50] Speaker 3 (maybe Samir): And there was also the private deploy environment running with a slightly outdated kernel + driver combo, which amplified latency on p95.

[01:05] Claire: Right, okay. Let's break that into two tracks. Samir, Marco — can you triage the kernel/driver mismatch and the router race within two weeks? We need firm owners and visible signals.

[01:18] Samir Bose (Head of Infra): On it. I'll create an infra ticket cascade and assign triage leads. We also need to run that KV cache experiment Marco mentioned — quantify when misses go from cheap to expensive.

[01:29] Marco: We're planning a KV cache benchmark across seq lengths; I'll run it with and without prefix caching to capture tail behavior. But I want product's input on where to prioritize — chat workloads or embeddings first?

[01:40] Tess Nguyen (Head of Product): My vote is chat first, especially customer-facing routes. Embeddings are high volume but chat is where tail latency really hurts perceived quality.

[01:50] Ravi Shah (Head of Research): One quick caveat — our quantized model variants show slightly different tail profiles; a KV miss coupled with a quantized kernel could amplify artifacts. I'll run comparative tests on our private infra. Should be a 4–5 day run.

[02:05] Claire: Good. Let's make that explicit in action items. Next — private deployments. Tess, give us the state of the roadmap and dependencies for SOC2 / compliance readiness.

[02:18] Tess: Sure. Short version: core work to enable private deployments is functionally complete for VPC peering and base KMS integration, but we have two gaps: audit log standardization and a hardened upgrade path (we need zero-downtime operator flows). Without those, enterprise customers will balk. There's also an ask from Legal to surface retention controls per-tenant.

[02:38] Aisha: Are we confident on timelines? Customers on the pilot list want an estimate in the next week.

[02:45] Tess: If we prioritize it, 6 weeks to a pilot-ready checklist — assuming we can allocate Samir's team for the upgrade path and Ravi for a quick quality gate.

[02:56] Claire: Leadership question: do we greenlight resources to push for that 6-week pilot? Pros: opens revenue for Dedicated/Private and addresses churn risk. Cons: pulls infra and research away from platform improvements. Thoughts?

[03:12] Marco: From engineering perspective, it's doable but we need a temporary reallocation. Without it, the pilot slips to Q1.

[03:20] Ravi: We can accelerate model gates but it'll mean cutting one medium-term infra improvement. Tradeoff is clear.

[03:28] Aisha: Financially, a successful pilot with 2 customers this quarter would justify the pull. I ran conservative numbers — runway covers it.

[03:36] Claire: Okay, rough straw poll — who supports greenlighting the pilot and reallocating resources? (pause) Looks like yes across the room. Let's make it a formal decision: pilot greenlit, list to be finalized by next Thursday.

[03:52] Samir: I'll coordinate infra commitments and post a schedule.

[03:56] Jordan Kim (EM Observability): Quick item on alerts — we've been flooded with noisy p95 alerts. I've been working on an alert tuning play to add per-route baselines and mute flapping. If infra will own the triage, observability will own the tuning.

[04:12] Claire: Perfect. Please land that in the next sprint and share an update in #observability.

[04:20] ---
[04:20] INCIDENT REVIEW DEEP DIVE (summary snippets):
[04:25] Marco: (Walkthrough) At 01:14 UTC on Aug 28, the router config push introduced a 200ms bump on p95 for 12 minutes, causing autoscaler to trigger incremental workers, which then tripped a placement constraint. We have logs that show a duplicated route key; likely a race with the deploy job.

[05:00] Claire: Questions? (someone asks about canary gating)

[05:07] Aisha: We didn't fully gate the canary with tail latency, that was on us — patching the gating.

[05:13] Tess: We'll add a canary metric specifically for p95 and failure rate.

[05:20] ---
[05:20] DISCUSSION: COST VS LATENCY TRADEOFFS
[05:22] Claire: On batching and caching, we're seeing incremental cost savings but some customers report odd hallucination profiles when we push aggressive quantization + batching. Ravi?

[05:30] Ravi: Those reports are real; quantized kernels can change output distributions subtly. We need a small quality-signal harness that runs perf and fnat tests on canary prompts. Quick signal in CI could stop bad rollouts.

[05:42] Marco: From ops side, intelligent defaults that bias lower latency for chat routes and cost-first for embedding routes would help customers self-select.

[05:48] Claire: Let's do route-level defaults + an expert mode. Tess, add to the product doc.

[05:55] ---
[06:00] HIRING AND PEOPLE NOTE:
[06:02] Aisha: Hiring is behind plan for SRE. My ask — authorize 2 contractor SREs for immediate coverage and speed hiring pipeline for full-time.

[06:10] Claire: Approved in principle. Aisha, send the budget scenarios; we need commit by next check-in.

[06:18] ---
[06:20] Q&A (rapidfire, with a few overlapping voices and filler)
[06:21] Claire: Any hard questions?
[06:22] Speaker 6: Will the pilot include encryption-at-rest options?

[06:24] Tess: Yes, customer KMS integration is on the list; HSM is a stretch but doable as an add-on.

[06:28] Speaker 2 (Jordan): For the alerting changes, will we keep the current noise threshold?

[06:30] Jordan: We'll reduce it by 20% but add smarter baselining.

[06:34] Aisha: On pricing — if we go to pilot, we should present a simple committed model and a surcharge for private infra ops. Finance will draft that.

[06:42] ---
[06:42] DECISIONS AND RECAP:
[06:43] Claire: Recap — 1) Greenlight the private deployment pilot, deliver pilot list next Thursday. 2) Infra triage and KV benchmarks owned by Samir/Marco within two weeks. 3) Observability will tune alerts and publish changes. 4) People: approve contractor SREs; hiring scenarios due end of month. 5) Product to publish prioritized top-3 features for next release.

[06:58] Aisha: I'll send meeting notes and action items after this — expect the postmortem link and the hiring scenarios.

[07:04] Claire: Thanks everyone. Quick morale note — we hit 1M API calls/day this month, team — please celebrate that win. Now, any blockers before we close?

[07:12] (brief chuckles, a couple of people say congrats)

[07:15] Marco: Nothing else from Eng.

[07:17] Tess: All good.

[07:20] Claire: Great — meeting adjourned.
